hero.description: A full-stack grocery price comparison prototype designed to make it easier to compare products across Greek supermarket websites and organise a shopping list without requiring an account.
hero.visualAlt: Implemented PriceWise compare-prices page in English, showing the navigation, hero message, search field and filters.

research.title: Price data exists, but not in one consistent place.
research.description: Greek supermarket sites differ in structure, naming, categories and availability. Comparing them manually takes time; engineering a unified view also requires collection, normalisation, storage and matching across inconsistent sources.
research.comparisonLabel: selected product price comparison as a desired feature
research.uiLabel: rated simple/easy-to-use UI as important or very important
research.accuracyLabel: said inaccurate or stale prices could make them stop using the app

ux.title: Research findings shaped the prototype.
ux.description: The thesis moved from questionnaire findings into requirements, personas, customer journey, Figma mockups, implementation and technical evaluation.

personas.giorgosDescription: Price-sensitive, comfortable with technology and wants fast product search, nearby supermarket filtering and an account-free list.
personas.mariaDescription: Needs to save time, compare familiar supermarkets and build a simple list she can optionally send by email.
personas.nikosDescription: Prefers clear search, readable prices and minimal navigation over feature-heavy workflows.

implementation.title: The working prototype, not just the Figma concept.
implementation.description: These screenshots show the implemented PriceWise interface: search and filtering, comparable product results, the supermarket comparison modal, the saved shopping list and the responsive mobile layout.
implementation.homeAlt: Implemented PriceWise home page in English with product search and category and store filters.
implementation.resultsAlt: Implemented PriceWise search results showing comparable 7Days products from multiple supermarkets.
implementation.compareAlt: Implemented PriceWise comparison modal showing the same product from Galaxias and Sklavenitis with prices and add-to-list actions.
implementation.listAlt: Implemented PriceWise shopping list with a saved product, price, supermarket, remove action and optional email delivery panel.
implementation.mobileAlt: Implemented PriceWise shopping list on a narrow mobile layout.
implementation.privacyAlt: Implemented PriceWise privacy page showing privacy information, navigation and footer.

designEvolution.title: Mockups were a starting point, not a frozen specification.
designEvolution.description: The thesis explicitly records implementation changes, including a product modal and visible EL/EN language switch added after the initial Figma work.

architecture.title: Separated frontend, backend, database and collection workflows.
architecture.scheduleDetails: Daily refresh rather than per-search scraping
architecture.uiRefreshDetails: Refresh connected clients after data updates

features.title: A deliberately focused prototype.
features.searchDescription: Search products and narrow results to selected supermarket chains.
features.listDescription: Store the list locally without mandatory account creation; optionally email it.
features.collectionDescription: Run supermarket-specific scrapers on a controlled schedule rather than every user search.
features.privacyDescription: Minimise personal-data collection and keep email delivery optional and consent-based.

quality.title: What was actually tested
quality.description: The thesis describes the technical evaluation as primarily manual testing. That distinction matters: Playwright was used for dynamic web scraping, not claimed as end-to-end UI test automation.

checks.backend: Backend endpoints, database connectivity and scraper behaviour
checks.errors: Error handling for incomplete or invalid cases

quality.futureTitle: Automated Jest tests were proposed, not fabricated.
quality.futureDescription: The thesis identifies unit and integration tests for data cleaning, product normalisation, API endpoints, shopping-list logic and frontend helpers as a future improvement.

items.0: Different supermarket HTML structures and JavaScript-loading behaviour
items.1: Selectors and scraping logic that can break when external sites change
items.2: Normalising and matching products with similar names but different quantities or brands
items.3: Keeping the multilingual interface clear without pretending product data is automatically translated
items.4: Balancing data freshness with responsible, limited scraping frequency

items.0: Improve product matching and comparison accuracy
items.1: Run focused usability tests with task-based observations
items.2: Add price history and threshold notifications
items.3: Explore a mobile app with offline shopping-list support
items.4: Add systematic unit and integration testing
